cim: Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights: Protecting Human Dignity in the Age of AI
cim_eredeti: Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights: Protecting Human Dignity in the Age of AI
szoveg_eredeti:
Human Rights Day, celebrated annually, highlights the universal principles of freedom, equality and human dignity enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

As the international community approaches the 80th anniversary of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, UNESCO, the Delegation of the European Union to the OECD and UNESCO, and the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan are convening a special event to explore the impact of artificial intelligence on human rights, cultural diversity, social cohesion and information integrity.

Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming the way people learn, communicate, create, access information and participate in public life. While offering unprecedented opportunities for innovation, inclusion and sustainable development, AI also raises important questions regarding human dignity, equality, freedom of expression, cultural diversity and the protection of fundamental rights.

The programme will feature the screening of The Beginning, an award-winning AI-produced film by Jordanian filmmaker Ibraheem Diab, inspired by true events. Through the story of a child fleeing conflict in search of safety, the film explores themes of war, migration, poverty, modern slavery, children's rights and human dignity, while illustrating how artificial intelligence can be harnessed as a creative tool to promote inclusion, cultural diversity, sustainable development and peaceful societies.

The screening will be followed by a high-level panel discussion bringing together representatives from UNESCO, the OECD, Member States and leading experts to discuss the role of AI in advancing human rights, peacebuilding, inclusion and information integrity.

The event will include the presentation of the publication Human Rights: Challenging 13 Common Misconceptions, jointly produced by UNESCO and the French National Consultative Commission on Human Rights (CNCDH), with the support of the European Union.

The event will also highlight the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, the first global standard-setting instrument in this field, and provide a platform for dialogue on how AI can be designed, developed and deployed in ways that are ethical, inclusive, human-centred and rights-based. Discussions will explore the implications of AI for peacebuilding, social cohesion and information integrity, while highlighting its potential to foster innovation, creativity, cultural diversity and sustainable development for the benefit of all.
